t: Founded at Ava by Nyaungyan Min, a son of Bayinnaung, after the collapse of the First Toungoo Empire in 1599.
Anaukpetlun took Syriam from the Portuguese in 1613; Thalun moved the capital back to Ava and ordered a revenue inquest.
Weakened by Manipuri raids and a Mon rising in 1740, it fell when southern forces took Ava in 1752.
dyk: Portuguese captives taken at Syriam in 1613 were resettled in Upper Burma as royal gunners; their Catholic descendants, the bayingyi, still live in villages there.
ev: Pegu falls and the First Toungoo Empire disintegrates
Anaukpetlun captures Syriam and executes Filipe de Brito
Chiang Mai is retaken and Lan Na returns to Burmese overlordship
Thalun moves the capital from Pegu to Ava
Thalun orders a kingdom-wide revenue inquest
The Burmese court hands the Ming Yongli Emperor to a Qing army
The Mon rise at Pegu and found the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom
Hanthawaddy forces capture Ava, ending the dynasty
